newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Clyde rejects Gulf Canada bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Clyde rejects Gulf Canada bid.

text.p: Clyde Petroleum Plc on Sunday advised its shareholders to reject a hostile 432 million sterling ($732 million) bid from Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, saying the offer drastically undervalued the company.
"Gulf Canada's offer dramatically undervalues Clyde on a cash flow multiple basis," chairman Malcolm Gourlay said.
"An independent Clyde will deliver a far better return for our shareholders than this low offer -- it's fairly much of a no-brainer to reject this offer," he told Reuters.

Releasing its defence document, Clyde said the bid put it on a cash flow multiple of 5.7 times, comparing unfavourably with comparable international companies trading on an historic (1995) multiple of 8.9 times and Gulf Canada on 12.7 times.

Clyde, which operates mainly in Britain, the Netherlands, Indonesia and Australia, said operating cash flow and profits, production and reserves, were all at record levels. The company was delivering sustainable, progressive dividends to its shareholders, it said.
Gulf Canada's cash offer of 105 pence per share was considered too low by many analysts when it was launched on December 18.
Shares in Clyde closed at 118 pence in London on Friday, indicating the market's belief that Gulf Canada would have to increase its offer to clinch a deal.
Gourlay declined to specify what he would consider a fairer valuation for Clyde.

Roy Franklin, Clyde's group managing director, said his company had been transformed in the past three years, and its strategy would create far greater value for shareholders than Gulf Canada's attempted takeover.
"Production, reserves, reported cash flow and reported profit have all consistently risen to record levels, and we've now got a business that is really performing," he told Reuters.
Clyde said daily net production in 1996 was estimated at 40,000 barrels of oil equivalent -- a rise of 77 percent since 1993.

Commercial reserves at December 31, 1996 were estimated at 130 million barrels of oil equivalent, an increase of 21 percent since 1993, while the total proven and probable reserve base had grown by 37 percent during the same period to an estimated 225 million barrels, Clyde said.

Before its bid in December, Gulf had made no secret of the fact that it was seeking an international acquisition which would bring with it a new core area to complement its extensive operations in Canada and Indonesia.
Clyde's activities in the North Sea and Australia made a good fit, analysts said.
Asked if Clyde had been approached by any other potential bidders, Gourlay said: "If we had an approach from somebody else, we would have to disclose that." ($1=.5899 Sterling)
